span.p: Deploy failed

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;
color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Nothing leaves the laptop without a rule
Push, PR, deploy, migration, env sync, DNS and webhooks are effects:
intent, approval, idempotency key and receipt
The harness pushes harness branches and opens PRs
It does not push main unless the developer turns that on
for a repo with no branch protection
Production deploy, live migration and DNS need approval each time
Preview and staging can be automatic

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Detect origin. GitHub first. GitLab later
Device OAuth, or an existing gh login, in the vault
Read branch protection and required checks
Default is PR mode. Direct mode pushes a branch the developer names

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Feature reaches DONE
Each PR, CI run and deploy is a ship_runs row

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
One push of harness/f/feature. Not one push per task
Open a draft PR from the graph: requirements, checks, migrations,
new dependencies, choices made for them, links to the plan
The structure needs no model. A summary paragraph is optional

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: GitHub Actions

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Mark the PR ready. Land as settings say
Required reviewers: wait. Never bypass them

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Read failed logs. Patterns first, then a small model
Platform difference: repair, and reproduce in the Tier D container
Missing secret: a human step. Never paste it into code
Flaky: re-run once, then the test owner
Real regression: repair task to the owning feature
Runner or quota: wait. No repair task
The worker sees the failing lines. Same fingerprint, 3 pushes, then the developer
Phase 0's CI workflow runs the same gates on Linux and Windows

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
One GitHub queue per account
Content-creating calls stay under 80 a minute and 500 an hour
Polling is conditional and backs off from 30 seconds to 5 minutes
retry-after and x-ratelimit-reset are obeyed
Repeated secondary limits pause the queue and show in the cockpit

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Which environment?

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Automatic. Test secrets. A disposable or branched database

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Automatic after the PR is ready, if staging is configured

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Explicit approval, with the plan shown

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
One adapter interface: probe, plan, deploy, status, logs,
promote, rollback, syncEnv
v1: Vercel and Docker over SSH
Railway, Fly.io, Render and AWS come later. No hosting yet is a discovery question. Nothing is created unasked

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Vault holds values per environment
syncEnv shows names only, and production needs approval
Production values are never pulled back for tests

div.style: color: rgb(21, 57, 45) !important; display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
0 Rehearse on a copy or a restored staging backup. Automatic
1 Backup or point-in-time recovery. Must succeed
2 Expand only: new tables, nullable columns, concurrent indexes
3 Deploy the app, which can read old and new
4 Batched backfill, with progress and pause
5 Contract in a later release, separately approved, export offered
A destructive migration cannot skip rehearsal and backup
A long lock switches to an online plan, or asks for a window

div.style: display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: After deploy

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Health and build ID. Smoke journeys with a test account
Watch errors for 10 minutes

div.style: color: rgb(64, 48, 11) !important; display: table-cell; white-space: nowrap; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center;

span.p: Result

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Mark released. Tag the commit. Notes from the graph

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Preview and staging roll the app back automatically
Production offers rollback, and does it only if that was enabled
The database stays. Expand-only changes are still compatible
A repair task gets the evidence

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p: Nothing switched. Logs attached. Repair task

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Webhooks, OAuth redirects and DNS are effects with receipts
An API call stores the returned ID so undo can remove it
Otherwise a guided human step, confirmed by a probe

div.style: display: table; white-space: break-spaces; line-height: 1.5; max-width: 200px; text-align: center; width: 200px;

span.p:
Developer commits on the same branch: merge, never force-push
A CI hour: back off, other work continues
Expired deploy token: reconnect, deployment parked

svg.text: Push, CI, deploy and live migrations
